question: Pri jednej bronzovej soche v starom meste v Bratislave stojí dopravná značka, pretože do nej autá opakovane narážali. Ako sa volá táto socha robotníka vykúkajúceho z kanála?

extra.why_interesting: Players know the statue as a cute tourist photo spot and assume it is just decoration. The twist is that it needs real traffic protection because drivers kept hitting it, and that is a funny detail most people walk past without noticing.
extra.verification_notes: Čumil is a bronze statue in Bratislava's old town with a traffic sign beside it; I did not find a source confirming that cars repeatedly hit it, and nothing contradicts the answer.

explanation: Čumil je taký nízko, že ho vodiči jednoducho prehliadali a viackrát ho poškodili. Preto má dnes vlastnú značku s nápisom „Man at Work“.

question: Andy Warhol, ktorého rodičia pochádzali zo slovenskej obce Miková, preslávil obraz plechoviek s jedlom, ktoré vraj sám jedol na obed dvadsať rokov. Čo bolo v tých plechovkách?
source_excerpt: Ondrej (aka Andrej) Warhola and Julia (née Zavacky) were immigrants from Miková in northeastern Slovakia.

extra.why_interesting: Players assume a world-famous artwork must hide a deep artistic idea. In fact it came from the artist's own boring lunch. Slovak players also get the bonus of a link to Slovakia that they can be proud of.
extra.verification_notes: Warhol's Campbell's Soup Cans and his remark about eating the soup for lunch for ~20 years are well documented, and his parents came from Miková (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_Warhola).

explanation: Warhol tvrdil, že dvadsať rokov obedoval stále tú istú polievku Campbell's, a tak ju jednoducho namaľoval. Jeho múzeum stojí neďaleko Mikovej, v Medzilaborciach.
